replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Evidence shows shared service credential execution; concrete escalation past per-analyst database grants."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Design shows LLM SQL executing before display; destructive/multi-statement SQL is a concrete tampering attack."},{"id":"T3","keep":false,"reason":"Same post-hoc-display weakness and same harm (harmful statement already executed) as T2.","duplicateOf":"T2"},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Shared credential plus post-execution SQL display supports distinct attribution-loss harm."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Free-form generated SQL running directly on shared analytics DB supports resource-exhaustion attack."},{"id":"T6","keep":false,"reason":"Repeats T1's attack (broad service credential, free-form SQL) and harm (reading credential tables).","duplicateOf":"T1"}]}
